purpose: Cyclosporine is used to prevent your body from rejecting a transplanted organ such as a kidney, liver, or heart. It is also used to treat severe autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis. An eye drop form is used to treat chronic dry eye disease.
how_it_works: Your immune system normally fights off things it sees as foreign, which is helpful for fighting infections but problematic when you have a new organ or an overactive immune response. Cyclosporine works by calming down a specific part of your immune system so it does not attack your new organ or your own healthy tissues. Think of it as turning down the volume on your immune system so it stops overreacting.
common_side_effects: High blood pressure, kidney problems, tremors or shaking hands, headache, increased hair growth on the body, swollen or tender gums, nausea, and an increased chance of getting infections. The eye drop form may cause a temporary burning or stinging sensation.
warnings: Because this medicine lowers your immune defenses, you are more vulnerable to infections and certain cancers, especially skin cancer, so avoid too much sun exposure. Your kidneys and blood pressure need to be checked regularly while you are on this medication. Do not take with grapefruit juice as it can raise drug levels dangerously. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications you take because many drugs interact with cyclosporine. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The dose is very individual and depends on your weight, the condition being treated, and your blood levels. For transplant patients it is typically taken twice a day by mouth. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to make sure the level in your body is in the right range — not too low to work and not too high to be safe. Always take it the same way each time, either always with food or always without food, and take it at the same times every day.
